name: Muong Hoa funicular
nameVi: Tàu hỏa leo núi Mường Hoa
kicker: Five-minute train to the cable station
summary: Mountain train from Sun Plaza: ride about five minutes to Hoang Lien station, toward the cable car. The line crosses two tunnels and four viaducts, and Vietnam Tourism describes it as the longest of its kind in Vietnam. It opened on 31 March 2018 and runs about 2 km. Buy this ride on its own. The cable-car ticket is a different purchase.

notice.title: Buy this ride on its own
notice.body: The cable-car ticket, the summit train, and this funicular are separate purchases. The fare is posted at the station.

body: The Muong Hoa train runs from Sun Plaza to Hoang Lien station, the stop for the cable car. The ride is about five minutes. It crosses two tunnels and four viaducts. Vietnam Tourism describes it as the longest of its kind in Vietnam. The line is about 2 km and opened on 31 March 2018.

This is the short train at the edge of town. The night train from Hanoi ends at Lao Cai. The cable car from Nguyễn Chí Thanh is the next ride, with its own ticket and its own clock. Pair the funicular with a cable-car day, and read that morning’s departure board before you buy.

gettingThere: The 2026 Fansipan guide sells the Muong Hoa train separately from the cable car and places the ride from Sun Plaza to Hoang Lien station. Vietnam Tourism describes the five-minute ride, two tunnels, and four viaducts. A published minute count from the church to Sun Plaza is missing.

legs.heading: From the stone church
legs.body: Go to Sun Plaza for the train to Hoang Lien station. Ask the minutes. The cable car starts at the station end.

closed: Weather can close the cable car, which is the reason most people ride this train. Check that morning.
admissionNote: The fare is separate from the cable car and from the summit train. A published funicular price is missing. Cable-car adult prices in print are 750,000 đồng on the 20 August 2018 operator page and 850,000 đồng round trip in the 2026 guide.
